chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, who said:

I was delayed from the Hajj, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What has delayed you from the Hajj?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, I guaranteed a man, but he shamed me (failed to pay).' He said: 'What is it to you and the guarantees? Do you not know that they destroyed the former generations?'
Then he said: 'A people committed many sins, so they feared them and feared a severe fear, and others came and said,
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the punishment upon them. Then the Blessed and High said: 'You feared Me and were audacious against Me.'

key_terms.خَفَرَ: To shame or fail to fulfill responsibility
key_terms.ذُنُوبُكُمْ عَلَيْنَا: Your sins are upon us (Quranic phrase)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on financial guarantees (kafalah) and their spiritual consequences according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) critiques the narrator's delay in Hajj due to *kafalah* (financial guarantee), linking it to the Quranic narrative of the Banu Israel where they declared 'Our sin is upon you' (Surah Al-A'raf 7:168), resulting in divine punishment. This illustrates the principle of vicarious liability in Shia jurisprudence, where assuming another's burden can lead to shared consequence, while also highlighting the spiritual danger of neglecting obligatory acts like Hajj for worldly guarantees.
